title: The finite-energy boundary of a group
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: Functions of finite energy on the Cayley complex of a finitely presented group, and the boundary they give the group. The first lesson sets up the Cayley complex of a presentation with relators of length at most three, proves that cocycles are gradients, defines the Hilbert space of finite-energy gradients and its subspace generated by finitely supported functions, bounds the interaction of two level cuts, and, when the two spaces differ, constructs a function with connected level sides. The second lesson, for a one-ended Cayley graph, embeds the group in a cube by the translates of that function and by functions recording the components of boxes, and proves that the closure is a compact metric space in which the edges have square summable lengths, that its boundary is a continuum with more than one point, and that vertices near a boundary point are joined by paths near it. The third lesson proves that the group acts on this boundary as a convergence group, compares g and gp for a parabolic fixed point p, and shows that every orbit is dense when the group is torsion-free. The fourth lesson proves that the boundary has covering dimension at most one, and that its first Čech cohomology vanishes when every 1-cochain on the Cayley complex with finitely supported coboundary can be corrected by a finitely supported cochain; so under these assumptions the boundary is locally connected only if it has cut points. The fifth lesson treats the case in which the boundary has cut points: from the tree of cut points it constructs a block of the boundary, a compact connected subset without cut points onto which the boundary retracts, of dimension at most one and with vanishing first Čech cohomology. The sixth lesson collects, for the boundary without cut points and for a block alike, the properties of the continuum, of a graph accumulating on it and of the group acting on both that the later arguments use. The seventh lesson prepares two tools for the continuum without cut points: component labels of the graph after deleting vertices, which are locally constant on the continuum, and an invariant system of annuli with the depth function that counts nested annuli. The eighth lesson studies the vertices of the graph of depth at least a given number: translates of a closed set by elements of large depth shrink to a point of the continuum, depths measured from them add up with a bounded error, and after such a translation any two points of the continuum other than that point get the same component label. The ninth lesson proves that the continuum without cut points is locally connected: beyond one depth, equal component labels stay equal at the next depth, so near a point of the continuum there are paths of the graph at every depth; their edges become short, and their limit points form a connected subset of the continuum. By the theorem on cut points of Peano continua of dimension at most one this contradicts the vanishing of the first Čech cohomology. The tenth lesson states the result as one theorem: for a triangular presentation with a one-ended Cayley graph, without elements of finite order, with the cochain condition for the group with two elements, and such that the group fixes a point of the dendrite quotient of the boundary whenever the boundary has cut points, every finite-energy gradient is a limit of gradients of finitely supported functions. It lists the lessons that prove it, and the statements that connect it with OpenAI's proof (2026) of the Singer conjecture in dimension four outside the middle degree and are not proved in the programme.
prerequisites: core course Functional Analysis (D20): closed subspaces of a Hilbert space, the Riesz representation theorem
core course Measure and Integration (D10): Tonelli's theorem, dominated convergence
free groups and presentations of groups
for the third lesson: the course Convergence groups (lesson Convergence actions and their elements)
for the fourth lesson: the course Continua, arcs and cut points, and covering dimension (Definition 2.1 of Covering dimension and finite trivializing covers)
for the fifth lesson: the course Convergence groups (lesson The tree of cut points) and, through it, the course Pretrees
for the tenth lesson: the course Convergence groups (lesson The fixed-point property for groups with one end)
the course proves every other fact it uses

checks.reading: Each proof was written out and re-read step by step on 11 Oct 2026 against Section 3 and Lemma found:gradient of OpenAI's preprint (library copy at commit adc7f124). Lesson 2 spells out the cases of degenerate cells in the count of components and the three properties of the small box in the proof of the path theorem. The exercises on Z, Z^2 and the free group were worked out by hand. Lesson 3 was written against Section 4 of the preprint; it adds a proof that a group with an infinite cyclic subgroup of finite index is not one-ended, and gives the constant 2 in the diameter bound. Lesson 4 was written against Section 5 of the preprint; it replaces Hausdorff measure by an elementary notion of length zero, states the cohomological hypothesis on the Cayley complex, works with any abelian coefficient group, and adds an exercise showing that the hypothesis fails for Z^2. Lesson 5 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against Section 7 of the manuscript (lemmas block:graph and block:near-path, proposition block:retraction); every step was re-derived; no gap found. The lesson states as hypotheses the two properties of the group that the tree of cut points needs and that have no provider in the programme. Lesson 6 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against the last part of Section 7 of the manuscript (proposition block:setting); each of the six properties was verified in both cases; no gap found. Lesson 7 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against Section 8 of the manuscript (lemmas ann:extension, ann:component, ann:system, ann:depth); every step was re-derived; no gap found. The extension across a point is taken from the lesson on Čech cohomology (Corollary 4.5). Lesson 8 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against the first half of Section 9 of the manuscript (lemmas push:shrinking, push:depth-comparison, push:component-labels, push:translated-deletions, push:eventual-labels); every step was re-derived; no gap found. Convergence of sets is stated without the Hausdorff metric (sets that shrink to a point). Lesson 9 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against the second half of Section 9 of the manuscript (lemmas push:majority, push:refinement, proposition push:local-connected) and the last step of its Section 10; every step was re-derived; no gap found. The limit of the paths is taken as the set of limit points of their vertex sets (Lemma 6.1 of the lesson), which avoids the compactness of the space of closed subsets. Lesson 10 was written on 12 Oct 2026: it assembles the earlier lessons into one theorem and compares with Sections 1, 2 and 10 of the manuscript, which were read for it. The fixed-point property for trees is taken from the course Convergence groups (lesson The fixed-point property for groups with one end) and is not a hypothesis of the theorem.

open_obligations: The translation between assumption (C_k) of the fourth lesson and the vanishing of the group cohomology H^2(Gamma; k Gamma) is not proved in the programme; it belongs to a course on group cohomology with group-ring coefficients, which does not exist yet.
The link between D_0 != D and a positive first L^2-Betti number is not proved in the programme; it belongs to a course on L^2-invariants, which does not exist yet.

Hypothesis (H4) of the tenth lesson (hypothesis (z) of the lesson The tree of cut points, course Convergence groups) has no provider in the programme: the group fixes a point of the dendrite quotient of the boundary. In the application it follows from Bowditch, Connectedness properties of limit sets, Lemma 1.4, whose proof needs group actions on real trees. The other hypothesis of the fifth lesson, the fixed-point property for trees with finite edge stabilizers, is proved in the course Convergence groups for groups with a one-ended Cayley graph.

The reductions from a finite aspherical Poincaré complex of formal dimension four to the hypotheses of the tenth lesson (statements (R1) to (R6) there: finite presentation and absence of torsion, Poincaré duality with group-ring coefficients, no splitting over finite or infinite cyclic subgroups, duality for L^2-Betti numbers) are not proved in the programme.
free_sources: OpenAI, The Singer conjecture in dimension four (OpenAI Math Release preprint, 25 Sep 2026), Sections 2 and 3
